issues.description: The HAS_TIME regex is an undocumented heuristic pre-filter whose contract with valueParser should be stated.
issues.detail: The regex /\dm?s/i acts as a fast-path before the authoritative valueParser walk. Its implicit invariant — if it returns false, no time token exists — is undocumented and must stay in lockstep with the parser's unit list. A one-line comment naming it as a cheap pre-filter, and noting that future time-unit additions must update both sites, would protect the abstraction.

issues.description: No test or fixture pins the early-return behavior or proves equivalence with the prior implementation.
issues.detail: The change is sold as behavior-preserving, but nothing exercises the awkward cases: time-like substrings inside url() or quoted strings, custom properties containing ms, vendor prefixes, or unusual whitespace and casing. A small fixture set demonstrating the early-return never skips a real violation would lock the optimization in and guard against quiet drift.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts this as a small, well-scoped performance patch: a cheap regex short-circuits the walkDecls callback before the heavier valueParser runs, preserving the rule's observable behavior. The only shared concern is that the HAS_TIME regex is an unstated second specification of "contains a time token" that must stay aligned with the parser, and the diff ships without a comment documenting that invariant or a fixture pinning the early-return. Both fixups are trivial and non-blocking. Land with a one-line comment and a guard test.
